prompt: A school orders $24$ boxes of pencils with $36$ pencils in each box. The office keeps $150$ pencils. How many pencils are left for the classrooms?
hint: This story has two parts. One part builds up a total and the other part takes some away. Decide which comes first.

hints.text: This story has two parts. One part builds up a total and the other part takes some away. Decide which comes first.

hints.title: 🪜 Try a simpler one
hints.text: If there were $2$ boxes of $36$, that would be $72$ pencils. Now scale the same idea up to $24$ boxes.
Find the total with $24 \times 36$, splitting it as $24 \times 30 + 24 \times 6$. Then subtract the $150$ pencils the office keeps.
$24 \times 36 = 720 + 144 = 864$ and $864 - 150 = 714$, so $714$ pencils are left for the classrooms.

explanation: First find how many pencils arrive in all: $24$ boxes of $36$ means $24 \times 36$.
Split the $36$ to multiply: $24 \times 30 = 720$ and $24 \times 6 = 144$, so the total is $720 + 144 = 864$ pencils.
The office keeps $150$ of them, so subtract: $864 - 150 = 714$.
That leaves $714$ pencils for the classrooms.
